source_snapshot.criteria: All information should match SPEC definition.

historical_reviews.deepseek: The BIOS operator requirement is correct, but its `modify`/read-write wording exceeds the row and cannot authorize a prefetcher change.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Classification and read-only boundary are accepted; OS telemetry is supporting only and log clearing is rejected.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code searches found no duplicate variant or completed record; adjacent Performance and topology pages do not supply this row's prefetcher oracle.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Hardware, adjacent-line and software prefetch controls may have separate labels and Auto/Enabled/Disabled meanings, so the expected matrix must identify each control rather than accept a generic page match.

original_test_intent: Have a qualified operator inspect every BIOS Advanced Prefetcher field and compare its displayed state with the CPU/platform-specific approved specification without changing any control.
original_method: Verify SUT, CPU family and BIOS/AGESA; enumerate the required prefetcher controls and Auto/Enabled/Disabled semantics; traverse the page read-only, capture each label/state and compare with the approved matrix; preserve logs and exit unchanged.
manual_activity: A qualified operator identifies and captures each hardware/software/adjacent-line or platform-specific prefetch control on the BIOS page and compares its current state with the approved CPU-specific matrix.
required_inputs: Exact SUT, board and CPU SKU/family
Complete page label and expected prefetcher state matrix
Auto, Enabled, Disabled, hidden and unsupported semantics
Protected evidence location and redaction policy
safety_requirements: Do not alter any prefetcher, CPU, memory, boost, power or performance setting
Do not infer a state from workload performance or OS telemetry
Do not clear dmesg, syslog or SEL
Stop on unexpected field, ambiguous Auto semantics, a changed setting or platform warning
No automatic retry or defaults reset
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the exact per-control comparison matrix
Support read-only CPU and firmware identity collection
Coordinate but do not claim BIOS UI control
Compare operator captures under owner-defined state semantics
engineer_actions: Approve the complete control inventory and expected states
Resolve discrepancies and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: NO/manual fits the BIOS UI dependency, but its modify/read-write wording does not match the source's information-only procedure.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Manual operator: verify CPU and firmware identity, enter Advanced -> Prefetcher settings, capture each displayed control/state and compare it with the approved matrix without changing anything.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Prefetcher page, information comparison and 20/20-minute estimates remain; no setting change or log clearing is permitted.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a matrix of exact BIOS label, prefetcher mechanism, expected state, Auto semantics, observed state and page evidence for the identified CPU/AGESA.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the unspecified SPEC oracle control-specific and removes DeepSeek's unsupported modification permission.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: OS counters or benchmark behavior cannot substitute for BIOS UI evidence and this row does not test functional performance impact.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Names and Auto behavior vary by CPU family and AGESA; a superficially matching label can govern a different prefetch mechanism.

project_override_considerations: A Project may define non-default prefetch policies, but the exact CPU/firmware-bound matrix must be approved before inspection. Functional enable/disable or performance delta testing is separate work requiring explicit mutation and workload controls.
expected_evidence: Approved prefetcher label/state matrix and Auto/optional semantics
Protected capture covering every page control
Preserved relevant boot/event evidence and no-mutation confirmation
Engineer-owned PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test Set, Procedure and Criteria consistently request an information check on the Prefetcher page. DeepSeek's modification wording is an over-broad reference interpretation, not a Master conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual inspection is defined once the owner supplies the CPU/AGESA-specific control matrix and a qualified operator can capture the BIOS page.

review_improvement: Defines each prefetch mechanism and state semantic, excludes unrequested mutation and prevents performance telemetry from replacing the BIOS page oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: Prefetch controls are not interchangeable: hardware stream, adjacent-line and software-related options can differ by processor generation and Auto may resolve through firmware policy. Accurate review therefore requires a label-to-mechanism-to-state mapping bound to the actual CPU and AGESA.
